analysis:
Reviewed the two head_text units of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1-801). The PR change is documentation only. Visible changes: lines 404-413 add Super eviction and pre-accept behavior (releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad, release of retained free KV segments and the MLX buffer cache once before eviction or refusal). The patch excerpt also adds a paragraph near head lines 1095-1115 on segmented paged admission, which parks free 64 MiB segments per pool outside the grant and ledger charge. That later text is outside the supplied units and the patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not review it.

No code, auth, crypto or protocol changes are in the supplied evidence, so no concrete security regression is identified.

Relevant threat IDs: T-041 and T-028 (residual KV data and prefix cache) and T-029 (resource availability). The parked free KV segments are retained memory outside the ledger charge. If they are not zeroed or reused only within the same size class, they could expose residual data across requests. The doc mentions 'new segments wrap zero-fil...', which is cut off.

A later pass should verify in the actual source (segmented paged KV pool code, not supplied) that:
- parked segments are cleared or fully overwritten before cross-tenant reuse;
- the parked memory, which sits outside the ledger, cannot starve other loads or evictions;
- the min(2 GiB, grant/8) bound is enforced.

The documented sequence from line 404 on (release before eviction, segments counted as reachable only until released) is consistent with the fail-closed admission gate and raises no concern.
